techniques.name: 7/4 Asymmetric Meter & Open D Pedal Point
techniques.description: Executing Dave Grohl's famous opening riff in 7/4 time (divided 4 beats + 3 beats) while maintaining a continuous ringing open 4th-string pedal tone with alternating high notes

notes: Pedal note: Open D string (4th string) picked continuously on eighth-note downstrokes
High melodic notes: Fret 7 on B string (F#) shifting to fret 5 (E) and fret 8 (G)
7/4 pulse: Count 1-2-3-4 (four beats) followed immediately by 1-2-3 (three beats)
sequence: Internalize the 7/4 meter by counting out loud at 100 BPM
Keep your fretting hand fingers arched high to avoid muting the open D string
Transition smoothly into straight 4/4 strumming when the drums enter
Layer aggressive downstroke power chords during the chorus for maximum volume impact
tips: Use a medium pick (0.73mm) to balance strumming flexibility on the chords with percussive riff attack
Let the open top strings ring across the Am7 and C chord shapes to create the signature Foo Fighters wall of sound
When shifting from 7/4 to 4/4, keep your internal clock steady—the tempo (145 BPM) does not change, only the bar length

beginner.title: Open Chords & 4/4 Chorus

Practice standard 4/4 strumming with energetic down-up motions at 145 BPM
Master switching cleanly between C, Em7, and D during the chorus

intermediate.title: 7/4 Counting & Intro Pedal Riff
steps: Count the 7/4 meter as a group of 4 followed by a group of 3 with a metronome
Practice alternate picking the open D pedal note against the fretted B string notes
Smoothly transition from the 7/4 intro riff into the straight 4/4 verse groove

advanced.title: Multi-Guitar Layering & Stage Dynamic Control
